Add on dips in GDDY and 6758 for defensive growth, and avoid KREN until volume confirms sustainability.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's mandatory biodiesel B40 and upcoming B50 mandates structurally lift demand for palm-oil-based energy and carbon credits, benefiting TPIA, CDIA, and TOBA.
Government push for domestic solar module manufacturing under the 2025 RUKN creates durable margin upside for local producers like NRG and BATR, insulating them from US tariff volatility.
Global carbon-market integration via JETP and Article 6 deals positions Indonesian geothermal and biomass players (BREN, HGII) for long-term premium revenue streams.
sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesian renewables names on local strength despite US drag; TPIA, CDIA, NRG lead on domestic policy momentum and earnings visibility. Favor integrated players with captive feedstock (BREN, BRPT) over pure developers. Trim exposure to US-linked climate-tech until Fed clarity; maintain WATCH for a breakout above +1% aggregate.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Small/mid-cap FMCG names are driving sector returns as institutional investors rotate out of large-cap staples into higher-beta consumer plays with clearer earnings catalysts.
Water and beverage companies (ADES, AGAR) are benefiting from structural demand growth in premium hydration and on-the-go consumption, supported by rising urban disposable income.
Packaging and plastics-linked consumer firms (PDES, INDR) are gaining on input-cost stabilization and export-driven volume recovery, offering durable margin expansion into 2025.
sectors.ai: Buy selective small/mid-cap FMCG names showing volume-price breakouts (PDES, ADES, AGAR) while large caps lag; momentum is broad but fragile, so take profits on 10%+ single-day spikes. Favor water/beverage and packaging sub-sectors for earnings visibility; avoid chasing BTEK without confirmation. Position for a 2-4 week hold as IDX consumer breadth improves, but trim if aggregate signal flips negative.

sectors.name: Logistics
themes: Domestic inter-island shipping demand is structurally rising due to Indonesia's commodity export diversification and new downstream processing hubs, insulating local logistics from US trade slowdowns.
Consolidation among small-cap logistics players (LOPI, ELPI, TAXI) is accelerating as fuel subsidy reforms and port efficiency upgrades favor operators with modern fleets and route density.
Air cargo (GIAA) remains a laggard versus sea freight as e-commerce growth shifts to lower-cost maritime last-mile solutions, pressuring yields and capping upside.
sectors.ai: Buy selective Indonesian logistics names on domestic momentum despite US weakness. LOPI, ELPI, and TAXI lead on volume and tariff-resilient intra-island demand; GTRA and BLTA offer steady bulk exposure. Favor small-cap movers over GIAA (air cargo laggard). Trim if IDX logistics breadth fades below +0.3% aggregate.
